title: QQ: Is 2-bit Enough? Exploiting Quantization to Enhance Computation and Memory Efficiency in Quantum Simulation
problem: Quantum computer simulations face significant computational and memory challenges due to massive floating-point arithmetic with complex numbers.
motivation: Reducing computational and memory overhead in quantum simulations enables scalable simulation of larger quantum systems.
method: Proposes integer-based quantization scheme (QQ) exploiting quantum gate matrix structure by separating real and imaginary components to eliminate zero-value operations. Achieves significant reduction in matrix-vector operations and memory.
key_novelty: Integer quantization scheme for quantum simulation exploiting gate structure to reduce arithmetic.
contributions: Integer-based quantization scheme for quantum simulations
Separation of real and imaginary components eliminating zero operations
Up to 50% reduction in matrix-vector multiplications
Up to 66.7% reduction in additions, 400,834× energy savings
limitations: Focus on 2-4 bit precision; behavior at other precisions not thoroughly explored.
primary_theme: Integer quantization for efficient quantum simulation
